A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 15-page ShowMak3r++ manuscript, including Appendices A-D. Text extraction and visual comparison establish matching research content, with no missing material.

before.justification: Section IV reports original reconstruction experiments and ablations, including quantitative results in Tables I-IV. Appendices C-D provide additional original qualitative reconstructions.

after.justification: Section IV and Appendices C-D retain the original quantitative experiments, ablations and qualitative reconstructions. These retained outcomes qualify as original empirical results.

M1.justification: Section III and Appendix B describe identical stage reconstruction, spatio-temporal positioning, ShotMatcher, actor reconstruction and face-fitting procedures. Components, losses and optimization schedules are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Sitcoms3D sitcoms, CMU Panoptic scenarios and web videos. Appendix D already includes Parkour2, Wonker, La La Land and CMIYC in v2; none is newly added in v3.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within corresponding experiments: HUGS, Shape-of-Motion, MonST3R, MegaSaM and earlier ShowMak3r in qualitative comparisons; Sitcoms3D, 3DGS, GS-W and FSGS in Table I; and ExAvatar in the facial comparison.

E3.justification: The stage evaluation still holds out 10 of 165 TBBT images. Panoptic still uses eight frontal cameras for stage reconstruction and one for actor reconstruction. Metrics, masking, cropping and training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The positioning, penetration-loss and face-refinement ablations remain identical in Tables II-IV. The trajectory, penetration and foreground-masking demonstrations in Figures 4 and 6 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both retain the same point-estimate and average reporting practices.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables I-IV and all qualitative result images are identical, including the appendices. For example, Ours retains PSNR 19.65 in Table I and 24.34 in Table II in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(21), their mathematical definitions and the MTED/MPED definitions are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion are identical. Both already claim ShowMak3r++ supports controlled TV shows and uncontrolled web videos, actor positioning and tracking, facial reconstruction and scene editing.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are identical. Section V retains the limitation that web-video background reconstruction covers only observed regions, and the appendices retain the same applicability statements.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same A6000 hardware, processing times, 6k-plus-2k alignment schedule and face-fitting architecture details. The project-page pointer and Appendix D source-video access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section II and all 86 references are identical. Positioning ShowMak3r++ as an extension of earlier ShowMak3r is already present in v2 and remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2, 26 March 2026, to v3, 20 May 2026. PDF author metadata adds Daeun Lee, already listed visibly in both versions; manuscript wording, terminology and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: All 17 figures, four tables and the algorithm display retain identical content, captions, placement and layout. Rendered pages match pixel for pixel outside the first-page arXiv stamp.

improvement.justification: The main text, methods, experimental evidence, result displays and Appendices A-D are identical. Updates to the arXiv stamp and administrative PDF metadata do not materially change the paper's scientific support, reproducibility or readability.
